Subject: Clarify charge quantum, smoothing and minimums for pilot pricing

Hi Emma — great to meet on Friday. Per our conversation you asked for a concise explanation of how we meter and round charges for short/interactive traffic, and how that ties to the pilot discount we discussed. Attaching a crude usage estimate you shared as input.

High-level ask: can you confirm the expected distribution of request lengths (input tokens and expected generated tokens) and whether most calls will be single-turn or multi-turn? That will change where we recommend smoothing vs per-request minimums.

To make progress internally we need to align on two things so we can finalize the term sheet:
- Billing quantum: how small requests are aggregated and the increment we charge (e.g., per-request vs conversation window).
- Pilot smoothing / minimum: whether Finexa needs per-call minimums or prefers a time-window aggregation (we offered both in the call).

If helpful I can propose one or two concrete metering rules we can include in the term sheet. Marissa and Marcus — looping you for pricing guidance if we want to firm an optional 12-mo commit + 15% pilot discount.

Thanks — Diego

Diego — thanks for the follow up and the attachments. Quick answers — most of our calls will be short (single question -> one-line answer), ~85% under 120 tokens generated, with the remaining 15% being longer follow-up flows (300-800 tokens). Volume: expect ~12k distinct users/day, approx 2 calls/user/day initially.

Two clarifying questions from procurement:
1) When you say "aggregation window" — will multiple short calls from the same user within e.g., 15 minutes be rolled up for charging, or do you charge strictly per API call?
2) On rounding quantum: if you round to e.g., 50-token buckets, does that apply to input+output combined or only output tokens?

On the pilot discount: procurement prefers to see a guarantee that smoothing won't materially overcharge compared to a pure per-call sum. If you can show a simple worked example for our usage profile that would help us move the term-sheet sign-off to legal.

—Emma

Subject: Re: Clarify charge quantum, smoothing and minimums for pilot pricing

Thanks Emma — that usage profile is very helpful. Below is a concise, actionable set of options we can put in the term sheet and a worked example. I'll call out where the smoothing/quantum impacts typical Finexa behavior.

Option A — Per-call metering (simplest):
- We charge input + output tokens for each API call, rounded up to the nearest 25-token increment.
- No aggregation across calls.
- Pros: perfectly aligned with per-API-call economics; cons: small, frequent calls see rounding overhead.

Option B — Conversation-window smoothing (recommended for your use case):
- We aggregate all calls from the same user identity (your user_id) within a 30-minute rolling window and bill the summed tokens for that window, rounded up to the nearest 100-token quantum.
- For multi-turn threads (continuations with parent message ids) we preserve context and do not double-charge cached KV tokens.
- Pros: reduces rounding overhead for bursty, short interactions; cons: slightly larger windows can mask micro-usage for analytics.

Option C — Session bucket (predictable commit-friendly):
- We offer fixed-size session buckets (e.g., 100k tokens / seat / month) with smoothing inside the bucket. Unused tokens from the bucket do not roll automatically (but we can add a partial rollover concession in a pilot).
- Pros: predictable cost; cons: requires accurate sizing.

Worked example (your profile):
- Assume 12k users/day × 2 calls/user = 24k calls/day. Average per-call input+output = 100 tokens.
- Per-call metering (Option A): each call rounded to nearest 25 -> many calls bill 100 -> 24k × 100 = 2.4M billed tokens/day.
- Conversation-window (Option B, 30-min, 100-token quantum): if 60% of short calls fall into windows with 2+ calls, aggregated billed tokens drop ~12–18% in our simulation (because two 100-token calls merge into one 200 -> rounded to 200 vs rounding each to 100).

Rounding specifics we typically apply (proposal):
- Rounding quantum applies to combined input+output tokens per aggregation unit (call or window).
- Default quanta: 25 tokens (per-call) or 100 tokens (30-min window). We can set custom quanta for pilots up to 10k tokens for large committed deals.
- Minimum billed per aggregation unit: 50 tokens (protects against spam/small malformed calls). We can waive/minimize this minimum for committed pilots with a higher discount.

Pilot commercial proposal (high level):
- 12-month pilot, committed monthly spend floor of $25k -> 15% list discount + smoothing set to Option B with 100-token window and 50-token minimum waived for the first 60 days.
- If you opt for a 24-month commit we can increase to 20% discount and add a one-time credit for initial usage estimation mismatch.

Ask for legal: if this sounds reasonable I'll prepare a redline-ready term-sheet with the concrete metering language and a short worked attachment showing day-1 vs smoothed billing under your sample data. Marissa: can you confirm discount approval for a 12-month $25k/mo floor? Marcus: any technical caveats on KV caching and how we show that in the worked example?

Best,
Diego

Quick technical note to include in the term-sheet/worked example — quoting so Emma sees the detail: 

On KV caching and double-counting: for multi-turn queries where the server populates local KV cache we do NOT charge again for tokens that are reused from KV for the same aggregation window. In other words, if user A sends message 1 (we generate 200 tokens), then user A sends a follow-up that reuses 150 tokens from the cached context, the follow-up's billed tokens reflect only the incremental generation plus any new input tokens.

Edge cases to mention explicitly: 
- Streaming completions: billed once per final token emitted; intermediate partials have no separate charge.
- Short probes (under 10 tokens of content): we protect against abuse by applying the 50-token minimum unless waived in pilot.
- Cross-user aggregation: we only aggregate by a provided stable user id or conversation id — we do not aggregate across different users even from the same IP.

I'll add a short appendix to the term-sheet with two worked CSV scenarios (per-call vs 30-min window) so procurement can validate the numbers. Marissa — confirmed that a 15% discount for a $25k/mo floor for 12 months is approvable from GTM/finance as a pilot concession.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
